description: Tag preset for MUSE reference analysis. The 4 layers (color/typography/layout/gradient) are used to produce tokens, and the visual_direction layer is used to generate the direction md.

tags.description: A subdued impression from lowered saturation. Marked by gray-mixed tones, low contrast, and a calm, restrained mood.
An impression pushed to maximum saturation. Marked by bright near-pure colors, a strong presence, and sharp, popping energy.
A bright, soft, low-saturation impression. Marked by white-tinted pale pink, mint, and lavender with a sweet, light airiness.
An impression of fluorescent light seeming to glow outward. Marked by electric pink, lime, and cyan over a dark background with a signboard-like radiance.
A sharp, acidic impression. Marked by lime yellow-green, fluorescent yellow, and excessive saturation that creates an uneasy beauty.
A sun-bleached impression. Marked by tones where saturation and brightness sink together, an old-photo texture, and a nostalgic mood.
A dark yet color-rich impression. Marked by deep, full tones like wine, forest green, and navy.
An impression dominated by warm colors. Marked by reds, oranges, yellows, and browns with the warm body-heat feel of sunlight.
An impression dominated by cool colors. Marked by blues, greens, and purples with a cold, clear, metallic airiness.
An impression of strong contrast colliding. Marked by white on black, a sharp clash of pure and achromatic colors, and a graphic tension.
An impression unified by a single color. Marked by varying only brightness and saturation within one hue and the static order of a restrained single tone.
An impression built from only two colors. Marked by simplified color planes like pink+blue or black+yellow over a photo and an editorial sensibility.
A palette impression drawn from soil and nature. Marked by terracotta, oak, olive, and sand tones blending into a warm, natural feel.
A deep, rich impression like gemstones. Marked by emerald, sapphire, ruby, and amber tones in a lustrous, luxurious contrast.
A palette impression drawn from the sea. Marked by aqua, teal, navy, and sand beige blending into a cool watery light.
A sweet impression like candy. Marked by bubblegum pink, mint, lemon, and lavender lightly mixed into a cheerful sweetness.
An impression drawn from the twilight sky. Marked by a warm orange-pink-purple gradient and the spread of sunset light.
An impression with a metallic sheen. Marked by chrome, gold, silver, and copper reflections and highlights creating a cold glint.
A traditional roman-type impression. Marked by stroke-end serifs, weight contrast, and a classic dignity suited to books and newspapers.
An early 19th-century sans-serif impression. Marked by slightly blunt forms, uniform stroke weight, and lowercase letters with closed apertures.
A neutral Helvetica-family sans-serif impression. Marked by cleanly horizontal or vertical stroke terminals, an emotion-free uniform weight, and a corporate/system tone.
A sans-serif impression based on circles and straight lines. Marked by a nearly perfect circular O, a single stroke weight, and architectural, modular forms.
A sans-serif impression retaining a handwriting rhythm. Marked by open apertures, slight stroke-weight variation, and warm, organic proportions.
A thick, rectangular serif impression. Marked by block-like decorative serifs, a strong headline presence, and the texture of Western posters and woodblock printing.
A high-contrast fashion-magazine serif impression. Marked by an extreme contrast between hairline strokes and thick vertical strokes, with thin flat horizontal serifs.
An impression where every character has the same width. Marked by a typewriter/code-editor feel, a fixed grid rhythm, and a technical, archival texture.
A connected cursive-handwriting impression. Marked by smooth curved connections, a slanted rhythm, and elegant swashes and terminal flourishes.
An impression of being written by hand. Marked by irregular line weight, a jagged baseline, and a personal, casual texture.
An exaggerated, decorative headline-only impression. Marked by extremely large size, a distinctive silhouette, and a strong personality hard to use for body text.
An impression of narrow, elongated compressed letters. Marked by vertically stretched proportions, dense blocks of text, and the impact of poster, sports, and news headlines.
An all-uppercase typeset impression. Marked by uniform letter height, block-like text masses, and a declarative, authoritative tone.
A magazine or publication-like impression. Marked by large serif headlines, dense body typesetting, a strong-contrast hierarchy, and a multi-column layout.
An impression aligned to a regular grid. Marked by consistent columns and rows, uniform spacing, and repeating same-size cells.
An impression of large and small boxes locked into a grid like a bento box. Marked by rounded-corner cards, cells of varying sizes, and one function per cell.
An impression that breaks left-right balance. Marked by a main element skewed to one side, a deliberately empty opposite space, and a dynamic tension.
An impression that deliberately violates the grid rules. Marked by overlapping elements, protruding blocks, misaligned placement, and a broken baseline.
A Pinterest-style bricklaying impression. Marked by variable-height cards, aligned columns with staggered rows, and a gapless pile of images.
An impression of identical modules repeated and assembled. Marked by same-size blocks, regular spacing, and a tidy, part-like fit.
An impression that halves the screen left-right or top-bottom. Marked by a clear dividing line, two contrasting regions, and typography on one side with an image on the other.
An impression of a huge visual anchoring the first screen. Marked by a screen-covering main image or video, a large headline, and a scroll cue at the bottom.
An impression of a visual filling all the way to the screen edges. Marked by margin-free edges, frameless images, and an immersion that flows past the boundary.
An impression of full-width sections stacked vertically. Marked by a run of full-wide blocks, clear separation between sections, and a long vertical flow.
An impression with a fixed vertical navigation on the left. Marked by a vertical menu column, a wide content area on the right, and the typical structure of dashboards and documentation sites.
A dashboard impression packed with widgets. Marked by many cards and charts shown at once, a density of numbers and graphs, and high information density.
An impression where scrolling drives the narrative. Marked by scroll-linked animation, section transition effects, and visuals that change as you progress.
An impression that unfolds horizontally. Marked by a left-to-right content track, horizontally arranged slides and project cards, and a lookbook/gallery format.
An impression of a multicolor light sheet flowing like an aurora. Marked by a dark navy base, vertical curtain light in pink, purple, cyan, and green, widely spread blur streaks, and a dreamy glow.

A mesh-gradient impression spreading from multiple points. Marked by an organic blend of 2-5 color points, borderless blob crossings, irregular color masses, and a composite blend that lends depth to 2D.
A metallic impression that reflects like a mirror or mercury. Marked by strong silver, gray, and black speculars, hard highlight contrast, and a cold, smooth reflective surface.
A warm-tone gradient impression spreading like a sunset. Marked by a horizontal transition from orange, coral, and pink into purple and navy, a warm-to-cool direction, and a single-axis blend.
A dreamy blur impression with fully dissolved edges. Marked by a background where large blobs are crushed with heavy blur, an out-of-focus haze, and low-contrast glowing clouds.
An impression of fluorescent color glowing on a dark base. Marked by high-saturation hot pink, lime, and cyan, a light source bleeding at the edges, and light spread and glow.
A radial-gradient impression spreading from center to edge. Marked by a bright core and darkening edges, a spotlight effect, and a circularly symmetric light-source feel.
An impression of a viscous liquid flowing. Marked by blob and droplet shapes, dripping or distorted outlines, organic curves, and fluid masses that imply motion.
An impression of an oil film floating on a wet surface. Marked by bands of teal, magenta, and gold rising over a dark base, a deep, glossy multicolor spread, and a dark iridescence.
An impression of film noise laid over a color spread. Marked by a smooth gradient base, a coarse grain texture, an analog feel, and a slightly dirty-looking surface.

visual_direction.token_mapping: reflected narratively in the visual direction document

genre.description: Era/cultural genre tags. Context tags that give compound direction across several technical layers.

tags.description: A chrome/liquid impression from around the year 2000. Marked by metallic reflection and gloss, inflated bubble forms, and a cyber, techno-optimist sensibility.
An 80s Miami neon nostalgia impression. Marked by pastel pink and cyan neon, a purple gradient, and a cyber sensibility.
An impression evoking 70s/mid-century nostalgia. Marked by mustard, burnt orange, avocado green, and chocolate brown blending together.
A roughly soiled impression. Marked by faded denim blue, murky khaki, and smoky gray blending with a scratched texture.
A 1920s-30s geometric-ornament impression. Marked by tall vertical proportions, a symmetric structure, and gold, geometric ornaments and line decoration.
A 1960s psychedelic-poster impression. Marked by wobbly curved lettering, a tightly packed space-filling layout, and intense complementary-color contrast.
A dot-graphic impression built from low-resolution pixels. Marked by angular square pixel units, a limited palette, a retro-game sensibility, and stepped outlines.
An impression that treats digital error as aesthetic. Marked by RGB channel separation, scanlines and datamoshing, torn pixel bands, and a CRT/VHS noise texture.
A handcrafted-texture impression unique to riso printing. Marked by 2-3 spot colors, misregistered color plates, coarse paper noise, and fluorescent pink and blue tones.
A retro-poster impression where print halftone dots are visible. Marked by a regular dot pattern, newsprint-style black-and-white or 2-color, comic-style shading, and a vintage print texture.

style.description: Style/mood tags. Design attitudes not tied to a specific era.

tags.description: An impression that exposes the raw as-is. Marked by system fonts, undecorated borders, rough alignment and deliberate crudeness, and exposed hyperlinks.
A pop impression of thick black outlines and vivid block colors. Marked by flat drop shadows, primary-color plane splits, tilted placement, and comic-style UI blocks.
An impression following the Swiss International Style tradition. Marked by a strict grid, left-aligned sans-serif, restrained color, and an objective tone.

An impression of a print-magazine spread transposed onto the screen. Marked by multi-column layout, a strong hierarchy between large headlines and body, and an editorial composition of photos and captions.
An impression of soft 3D objects like clay or jelly. Marked by rounded corners, subtle shadows, a matte surface, and pastel-color character.
An impression of looking through frosted glass. Marked by translucent cards over a blurred background, faint color refraction, and a thin highlight border.
An impression of multicolor reflection like holo foil. Marked by a metallic sheet shimmering in pink, mint, lavender, and cyan, a rainbow gloss surface, and angle-dependent reflected light.

An impression of subtly shifting color like a pearl or soap bubble. Marked by a shallow crossover of satin white, lilac, champagne, and teal, a low-saturation gloss, and a subtle angle-dependent shift.
A 3D style where angular polygon faces are exposed. Marked by simplified geometric faces, flat shading, a limited color palette, and an origami-like texture.
A 3D impression rendered like cel animation. Marked by thick black outlines, stepped cel shading, flat color regions, and a comic sense of volume.

A 3D illustration impression drawn in isometric projection. Marked by simultaneous front and side exposure at a 30-degree tilt, an architectural/diagrammatic sense of space, flat color, and clean face splits.

subject.description: Visual subject type. The main visual element that dominates the screen.

tags.description: An impression where a 3D object rendered in CG software is the subject. Marked by realistic lighting and shadow, dimensional volume, and material reflection.
An impression where a flat vector illustration is the subject. Marked by shadowless color planes, simple silhouettes, a limited palette, and clean outlines.
A hand-drawn doodle or sketch impression. Marked by uneven ink lines, rough bleeds, pencil and marker texture, and deliberately crooked forms.
A magazine editorial-style collage impression. Marked by cut-and-pasted photo fragments, torn paper edges, a jarring juxtaposition of typography and image, and a scrapbook texture.
A photographic impression where a person's face occupies the screen. Marked by a shallow-depth close-up, skin detail, emotional expression, and studio or natural lighting.
A photographic impression of a physical product shot in a studio. Marked by a clean background, tidy highlights and shadows, emphasized material detail, and an advertising composition.

An impression where oversized typography itself is the subject. Marked by a page-covering wordmark, overwhelming letter size, typesetting that cuts through whitespace, and a composition of words alone with no image.

An impression where letters are transformed and distorted into sculptural forms. Marked by stretched or melted letterforms, 3D-ified letters, pixel and glitch effects, and rule-breaking custom typefaces.

An impression where abstract shapes are the subject with no concrete object. Marked by blob and geometric forms, exaggerated color blocks, objects floating in space, and a form-first composition over meaning.
A screenshot impression that shows the product screen itself. Marked by a real interface frame, dashboard and app layouts, exposed data and components, and often a dark-mode glow treatment.
An impression of UI held inside a device frame like an iPhone or MacBook. Marked by the silhouette of product hardware, a tilted 3D perspective, glass reflection, and a hand-held composition.

A feature-showcase impression with uneven cards tiled together. Marked by rectangular splits of different sizes, a different visual per cell, rounded-corner cards, and an Apple-style feature-introduction composition.
An impression where a tidy icon set composes the screen. Marked by uniform stroke and size, simplified pictograms, grid alignment, and systematic repetition.
An impression covered entirely in film noise. Marked by a fine grain texture, slight color bleed, an analog-photo sensibility, and flat color with a felt texture.
